definitions.explanation: Height measured from mean sea level. Used to express the elevation of land, mountains, or locations.

examples.japanese: {海抜|かいばつ}ゼロメートル⟦{地帯|ちたい}→地帯：04057_chitai⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{海抜|かいばつ}⟦{約|やく}→約：09563_yaku⟧500⟦メートル→メートル：02975_meetoru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: This town is at about 500 meters above sea level.

examples.japanese: ⟦{富士山|ふじさん}→富士山：09514_fujisan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{山頂|さんちょう}→山頂：09942_sanchou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{海抜|かいばつ}3,776⟦メートル→メートル：02975_meetoru⟧で、⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{最|もっと}も→最も：01736_mottomo⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧。
examples.english: The summit of Mt. Fuji is 3,776 meters above sea level, the highest in Japan.

notes:
FORMS:
{海|かい} (sea) + {抜|ばつ} (above, exceeding). Literally "above the sea."

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {海抜|かいばつ}〜⟦メートル→メートル：02975_meetoru⟧: ... meters above sea level
- {海抜|かいばつ}ゼロメートル⟦{地帯|ちたい}→地帯：04057_chitai⟧: areas at or below sea level (flood risk zones)

CONTRAST WITH {標高|ひょうこう}:
- {海抜|かいばつ}: general term, commonly seen on signs and in everyday descriptions
- ⟦{標高|ひょうこう}→標高：13175_hyoukou⟧: more technical, preferred in geography, mountaineering, and scientific writing
- Both measure height from sea level, but ⟦{標高|ひょうこう}→標高：13175_hyoukou⟧ is more precise in academic contexts

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {海抜|かいばつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧: high elevation
- {海抜|かいばつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{低|ひく}い→低い：02947_hikui⟧: low elevation
- {海抜|かいばつ}⟦{表示|ひょうじ}→表示：03143_hyouji⟧: elevation sign (often seen on utility poles in flood-prone areas)
